comments.author: @travellives
comments.text: Anguilla's story reaches far beyond its beaches. What stayed with you most: the fight for change in 1967, the realities of everyday life, or the unexpected .ai economy? If you know Anguilla, we'd love to hear what you would add.

comments.author: @lifeonearth68
comments.text: I never knew Anguilla had a history of salt harvesting. It's amazing how much the island's economy has changed. Does anyone there still harvest salt the traditional way? 😇😇

comments.author: @Caribbeandetour
comments.text: The high-end tourism has always been a staple since Malliouhana and Cap Juluca hotels. The day trippers numbers has increased significantly in recent years.

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: That shift towards more day trippers has definitely changed the rhythm of the tourism industry on the island recently. ✨

comments.author: @UnseenOutlands
comments.text: Anguilla's luxury resorts look incredible, but I'm curious about the people whose work keeps the tourism industry running. Do hotel employees, construction workers, drivers, and small business owners benefit equally from the island's success as a high-end destination? What challenges do local families face when tourism is seasonal and living costs remain high?

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: Families manage these economic shifts by balancing seasonal tourism income with local entrepreneurship, though the high cost of living remains a daily reality for many workers in the industry. ✨

comments.author: @ZanderGordonn
comments.text: I knew Anguilla for its beaches, but I had no idea about the struggle with St. Kitts. That history gives the island a whole different meaning.

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: It adds so much context to life there today. The people wanted more say in their island’s future.
